title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Regulations on the Work of Special Supervisors of the Supreme People's Court
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Circular of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Regulations on the Work of Specially-Appointed Supervisors of the Supreme People's Court

Fa [2012] No. 173

To: the Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region

The Regulations on the Work of Specially-Appointed Supervisors of the Supreme People's Court have been reviewed and adopted at the meeting of the Party Leadership Group of this Court. They are hereby issued for your careful study and for your support and cooperation in the work.

July 13, 2012

Regulations on the Work of Specially-Appointed Supervisors

To further improve and perfect the external supervision mechanism of the people's courts, safeguard judicial fairness, enhance judicial credibility, and promote the scientific development of the work of the people's courts, these Regulations are formulated in accordance with work needs.

Article 1. Specially-Appointed Supervisors of the Supreme People's Court are persons engaged by the Supreme People's Court from among deputies to the National People's Congress, members of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, various democratic parties, the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce, personages without party affiliation, experts and scholars, and grassroots masses, to supervise the adjudication, enforcement, team building and other work of the Supreme People's Court and to put forward opinions and suggestions.

Article 2. Specially-Appointed Supervisors of the Supreme People's Court shall be recommended by relevant organizations, and the consent of the person concerned and his or her unit must be obtained.

The Supreme People's Court shall issue letters of appointment and "Specially-Appointed Supervisor Cards" to the engaged Specially-Appointed Supervisors, and shall make the information public.

The term of office of each Specially-Appointed Supervisor of the Supreme People's Court shall be five years. Additions may be made when necessary according to work needs.

If a Specially-Appointed Supervisor requests in writing to resign from the position during the term of office, he or she shall be removed from the post by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 3. The work of Specially-Appointed Supervisors of the Supreme People's Court shall adhere to the principles of lawfulness, orderliness, pragmatism, and effectiveness.

Article 4. The duties of Specially-Appointed Supervisors of the Supreme People's Court are:

(1) to supervise the Supreme People's Court's implementation of laws and regulations and its making of judicial decisions;
(2) to supervise the situation of the staff of the Supreme People's Court in adjudication and enforcement work regarding impartial administration of justice;
(3) to supervise the situation of the staff of the Supreme People's Court in terms of adjudication style, integrity and self-discipline, and compliance with judges' professional ethics; and
(4) to supervise other relevant matters.

Article 5. The methods by which Specially-Appointed Supervisors of the Supreme People's Court perform their duties are:

(1) attending, upon invitation, relevant work meetings of the Supreme People's Court;
(2) participating in specialized meetings of Specially-Appointed Supervisors convened by the Supreme People's Court;
(3) observing the trial activities of cases publicly tried according to law;
(4) attending, upon invitation, special inspection activities organized by the Supreme People's Court concerning adjudication, enforcement, team building and other work;
(5) reflecting or forwarding criticism, opinions, suggestions, or report materials from the masses against the people's courts or court staff;
(6) hearing and learning about the handling of matters such as opinions, suggestions, and reports submitted; and
(7) other lawful and effective methods of supervision.

Article 6. Specially-Appointed Supervisors of the Supreme People's Court shall keep confidential the secrets of adjudication and enforcement work when carrying out their work, and shall not use the status of Specially-Appointed Supervisor to engage in activities inconsistent with the work of supervisors.

Article 7. All departments of the Supreme People's Court shall actively assist, cooperate with, and support Specially-Appointed Supervisors in exercising their supervisory powers in accordance with these Regulations, earnestly listen to opinions and suggestions, respond to inquiries, and handle and give feedback on matters reflected or forwarded in a timely manner. Whoever obstructs a Specially-Appointed Supervisor from performing his or her duties, refuses to accept supervision, or retaliates against a Specially-Appointed Supervisor shall be dealt with seriously in accordance with relevant laws and discipline.

Article 8. The People's Supervision Work Office of the Supreme People's Court shall be responsible for the routine administrative work concerning Specially-Appointed Supervisors.

Article 9. These Regulations shall take effect as of the date of promulgation, and the General Office of the Supreme People's Court shall be responsible for their interpretation.
